To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ogg1 and/or Nth1 do not contribute to Ig class switching in activated B cells.
the DNA glycosilases Ogg1 or Nth1 are not required for the generation of DNA breaks or for Ig class switching in activated B cells.
the DNA glycosyles Ogg1 and nth1 do not contribute to Ig class switching in activated mouse splenic B cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of deletion or mutation of the DNA glycosyles Ogg1 and/or Nth1 on DNA breaks in the IgH S regions and c-myc gene in activated mouse splenic B cells.
the effect of DNA glycosylase deficiency on DNA damage in B cells and on class switching.
the repair of DNA breaks in the IgH locus in splenic B cell class switching, and our data suggest that these DNA glycosylase activities are not involved in the repair of these breaks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ogg1- and Nth1-mediated base excision repair (BER) does not contribute to class switching or DSB formation in the S regions of the IgH locus or the c-myc locus in activated splenic B cells.
the Ogg1 and/or Nth1 DNA repair pathways do not play a major role in IgH class switching in activated splenic B cells.
the DNA glycosylation pathway is not required for Ig class switching in splenocytes.

the DNA glycosyles Ogg1 and/or Nth1 do not contribute significantly to the formation of S region and c-myc DNA DSBs during class switching in activated splenic B cells.
the two DNA glycosylase genes Ogg1 and/or Nth1 do not appear to be essential for class switching or for DSB formation in activated splenic B cells.
Ogg1 and/or Nth1 do not contribute to the formation of S region or cmyc DSBs during class switching.
